records.verbatim definition: A Process is a repetitive activity that may be cross-functional and measurable and that may perform a task with customer focus. The processes are used for many levels of complexity from high, general levels down to lower, more detailed levels. There are certain processes that are not refinable, for example stores, which are visualized as a triangle. The process is named with a verb and a noun that describe what happens, e.g. build cars, bake bread, print document and so on.
records.normalized explanation: A repeatable, measurable, customer-focused activity that can span functions and be refined across levels; non-refinable processes such as stores use a triangle.
records.visible symbol description: Base symbol: white horizontal process shape with a concave left notch and pointed/indented right end. Alternatives shown: blue diamond Decision/choice, white rectangle Activity, white oval Operation, and two Stock triangle orientations.
records.context or perspective: Process modeling across general and detailed levels.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Processes may be refined from high/general to lower/more detailed levels. A non-refinable process is represented by a triangle.
explicitly allowed uses: Name with a verb and a noun.
Use across multiple levels of process complexity.
Use a triangle for processes that are not refinable, for example stores.
explicitly stated restrictions: No connector cardinality or execution semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: A Decision is a type of process with a special symbol that shows that a decision of choice has to be made where different alternatives can be described. A decision can be named under a process but one ought to be able to respond with different alternatives such as for example Buy Car: Yes/No, Product is faulty: Stop production/Let it go, Purchase plant: alternative a/b/c.
records.normalized explanation: A process-type item representing a choice among described alternatives.
records.visible symbol description: Blue diamond, labeled Decision/choice in the table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No explicit containment rule beyond being a type of process.
explicitly allowed uses: Describe a decision or choice with alternatives.
May be named under a process.
explicitly stated restrictions: The printed alternatives are examples, not a complete validation rule.

records.verbatim definition: No separate prose definition is printed in the uploaded pages; Activity is shown as an alternative symbol in the Process row.
records.normalized explanation: An alternative process symbol whose exact semantics are not defined in these pages.
records.visible symbol description: White rectangle labeled Activity.
records.context or perspective: Shown only in the Process alternatives table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Unresolved.
explicitly allowed uses: Visually presented as an alternative process symbol.
explicitly stated restrictions: No explicit definition, naming rule, refinement rule, or relation rule is stated for Activity in the uploaded pages.

records.verbatim definition: No separate prose definition is printed in the uploaded pages; Operation is shown as an alternative symbol in the Process row.
records.normalized explanation: An alternative process symbol whose exact semantics are not defined in these pages.
records.visible symbol description: White horizontal oval labeled Operation.
records.context or perspective: Shown only in the Process alternatives table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Unresolved.
explicitly allowed uses: Visually presented as an alternative process symbol.
explicitly stated restrictions: No explicit definition, naming rule, refinement rule, or relation rule is stated for Operation in the uploaded pages.

records.verbatim definition: No separate prose definition is printed in the uploaded pages; Stock is shown as an alternative symbol in the Process row.
records.normalized explanation: A non-refinable process/store symbol; the exact distinction between the two triangle orientations is not stated.
records.visible symbol description: White triangle pointing upward, labeled Stock.
records.context or perspective: Shown in the Process alternatives table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: The Process definition states that processes that are not refinable, for example stores, are visualized as a triangle.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a process that is not refinable, for example a store.
explicitly stated restrictions: The meaning of upward versus downward triangle orientation is unresolved.

records.verbatim definition: No separate prose definition is printed in the uploaded pages; a second Stock symbol is shown as an alternative symbol in the Process row.
records.normalized explanation: A second visible Stock triangle; its distinct meaning, if any, is not stated.
records.visible symbol description: White inverted triangle pointing downward, labeled Stock.
records.context or perspective: Shown in the Process alternatives table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: The Process definition associates triangles with non-refinable processes such as stores.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a process that is not refinable, for example a store.
explicitly stated restrictions: The meaning of upward versus downward triangle orientation is unresolved.

records.verbatim definition: Business object is a refinement or resource object in the form of a physical object or a processed product, or an information package. (It may even sometimes be an abstract entity (see: Need for Adjustment) related to a process). If you need to demonstrate that a document that is described, then there is a new format in the business object that has an asymmetric right corner. The business object is given a noun and often has the addition of an adjective or participle before the name (Frozen meatballs, vegetables delivered, document template).
records.normalized explanation: A process refinement/resource item representing a physical object, processed product, information package, and sometimes an abstract entity.
records.visible symbol description: Base symbol: solid blue square. Document alternative: white document-like shape with an asymmetric right corner.
records.context or perspective: Prerequisite, result, resource, product, information package, or abstract entity related to a process.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Can serve as prerequisite, refinement result, supporting object, side effect, or verifying documentation depending on relation and context.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent physical objects, processed products, information packages, and sometimes abstract entities related to a process.
Use the document alternative when demonstrating a described document.
Name with a noun, often preceded by an adjective or participle.
explicitly stated restrictions: No universal connector meaning is defined independent of context.

records.verbatim definition: If you need to demonstrate that a document that is described, then there is a new format in the business object that has an asymmetric right corner.
records.normalized explanation: A Business object visual variant used for a described document.
records.visible symbol description: White document-like symbol with an asymmetric right corner.
records.context or perspective: Document representation within the Business object category.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: A visual subtype/format of Business object; no separate containment semantics are stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Use when a described document needs to be demonstrated.
explicitly stated restrictions: No independent model-item semantics beyond the Business object definition are stated.

records.verbatim definition: A Requirement in terms of Business Modeler is a specific quality defined for a process, business object (result) or role described by an interested party or organization or process. A requirement is named by indicating its direction (increase / decrease) or level of a specific quality for example improved regularity, reduced waste.
records.normalized explanation: A specific quality target for a process, Business object/result, or role, stated by an interested party, organization, or process.
records.visible symbol description: White hexagon outlined in orange.
records.context or perspective: Quality requirement applied to a process, result, or role.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Define a specific quality for a process, Business object/result, or role.
Name by direction or level of a quality, such as increase/decrease or improved/reduced.
explicitly stated restrictions: No numeric threshold, cardinality, or validation rule is stated.

records.verbatim definition: A Position is a position in an organizational department. A position may comprise one or more roles. The position is the relation between a specific organization and the roles required in that organization. The position is titled with the comprehensive organizational prefix, for example Purchasing manager, Logistics supervisor.
records.normalized explanation: An organizational position connecting a specific organization to one or more required roles.
records.visible symbol description: Two outlined human figures, one behind or next to the other.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: May comprise one or more roles; relates a specific organization to required roles.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a position in an organizational department.
Title with a comprehensive organizational prefix.
explicitly stated restrictions: No formal maximum number of roles is stated.

records.verbatim definition: An Interested Party is a higher level of role. The interested party is used to show relationships between general groups of organizations and/or individuals are perceived. If one wants to demonstrate that an individual is an interested party, there is an alternative symbol that resembles an ‘Interested party’ but has two individuals inside it, for example customers. When naming an interested party the central part of the model should be used, for example MBM customers, XXX owner(s).
records.normalized explanation: A high-level role used to show perceived relationships among general groups of organizations and/or individuals.
records.visible symbol description: Base symbol: white horizontal oval outlined in orange. Alternative Team symbol: orange-outlined oval containing two human figures.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Can conceptually group organizations and/or individuals; precise containment semantics are not stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Show relationships between general groups of organizations and/or individuals.
Use the alternative two-person symbol when demonstrating that an individual is an interested party.
Name from the central part of the model, e.g. MBM customers, XXX owner(s).
explicitly stated restrictions: No formal membership cardinality is stated.

records.verbatim definition: If one wants to demonstrate that an individual is an interested party, there is an alternative symbol that resembles an ‘Interested party’ but has two individuals inside it, for example customers.
records.normalized explanation: An Interested Party alternative showing people inside the oval.
records.visible symbol description: Orange-outlined oval containing two human figures; labeled Team in the table.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No explicit membership cardinality beyond the visible two-person icon.
explicitly allowed uses: Use when demonstrating that an individual is an interested party.
explicitly stated restrictions: The two figures are a symbol design and do not establish cardinality.

records.verbatim definition: An Organization is an abstract unit used to specify a specific organization department with defined targets and resources. The naming of organizations is most often done in accordance with the most important process, for example engine development (avoid numerals).
records.normalized explanation: An abstract organizational unit with defined targets and resources.
records.visible symbol description: Yellow folder-like icon.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No explicit containment rule in the definition; relations may describe organizational structure.
explicitly allowed uses: Specify an organization department with defined targets and resources.
Name most often according to the most important process.
explicitly stated restrictions: Avoid numerals in organization names.

records.verbatim definition: An Individual is a person – a specific individual. There are icons for men and women. When naming individuals use real names, not codes!
records.normalized explanation: A specific person.
records.visible symbol description: Yellow male and female person icons.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No hierarchy or containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a specific individual.
Use real names.
explicitly stated restrictions: Do not use codes when naming individuals.

records.verbatim definition: A Role is an abstract composition of competence profile as required by the different processes. Roles may be collected to cover a position. A role is named in conjunction with the competency profile as defined by the process, for example system development, project manager, IT expert, catalyst.
records.normalized explanation: An abstract competence profile required by processes; roles may be collected into a Position.
records.visible symbol description: Yellow top-hat icon.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Roles may be collected to cover a Position.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent competence profiles required by processes.
Name in conjunction with the competency profile defined by the process.
explicitly stated restrictions: No minimum or maximum number of roles per Position is stated.

records.verbatim definition: A Project is an abstract object to show and describe a specific project. A project is something one does once only and that has a defined start and a defined finish and a measurable target and an approved budget. The project is named as per the organization, often with a verb and a noun, for example Project XXX, Recovery of waste-heat.
records.normalized explanation: A one-time undertaking with defined start and finish, measurable target, and approved budget.
records.visible symbol description: Yellow curved arrow.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No hierarchy or containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a specific one-time project.
Name according to the organization, often with a verb and noun.
explicitly stated restrictions: Must be done once only and have defined start, finish, measurable target, and approved budget according to the printed definition.

records.verbatim definition: An Action is a detailed level of a sub-process that describes the common denominator between the business activities and computerized applications, i.e. the utilization of objects and methods, or the use of pre-existing IT methods through messaging. Actions are described in both process models and IT-models. The name must reflect the required action. Use a verb plus the object that is involved in the action. A strict standard is recommended as the actions name will probably appear as menu choices in later implemented application such as order, new user, update customer.
records.normalized explanation: A detailed subprocess-level item bridging business activity and computerized application behavior.
records.visible symbol description: White rounded rectangle.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: A detailed level of a sub-process; may appear in both process models and IT-models.
explicitly allowed uses: Describe object or method utilization or use of existing IT methods through messaging.
Use in both process models and IT-models.
Name with a verb plus the involved object.
explicitly stated restrictions: No executable application schema is defined.

records.verbatim definition: An Object is an IT component that contains a collection of independent, well-defined collated data and corresponding logic, or ‘information’. The logic is divided into methods. A method is also a well-defined logical share and an object. The logic will indicate working with the stored information. A method may also call in other methods through objects or can communicate through ‘messaging’. An object is activated by the issue of an order which addresses requirements. An order can be made from an action or an object. When naming an object it must be the same as the agreed name of the business object. An object shall have the same conventions as for actions, for example New XXX, update XXX, Remove XXX.
records.normalized explanation: An IT component containing collated data or information and corresponding logic divided into methods, activated by orders from actions or objects.
records.visible symbol description: White square outline.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Contains data or information and corresponding logic or methods; may call methods through objects or communicate by messaging.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent an IT component with data and logic.
Activate by an order addressing requirements.
Orders may originate from an action or an object.
Use the agreed Business object name.
Use action-like naming conventions.
explicitly stated restrictions: The wording around object naming and examples is internally difficult to reconcile and is retained verbatim.
No software class schema is inferred.

records.verbatim definition: An Application is an information system that supports a process/action. Most often used in process and IT-models. There is an extra symbol here that shows if it is an archive that one is talking about. Naming in accordance with traditional usage within the organization.
records.normalized explanation: An information system supporting a process or action; an alternative symbol denotes an archive.
records.visible symbol description: Base symbol: gray cylinder with blue top. Alternative Archive: white window or document-like icon with a blue title bar.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Support a process/action.
Use most often in process and IT-models.
Use the extra archive symbol when referring to an archive.
Name according to traditional organizational usage.
explicitly stated restrictions: No application schema, renderer rule, or software architecture semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: There is an extra symbol here that shows if it is an archive that one is talking about.
records.normalized explanation: An Application alternative used to show an archive.
records.visible symbol description: White rectangular window or document icon with a blue title bar; labeled Archive in the table.
records.context or perspective: Archive representation in process and IT-models.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No separate containment meaning is stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Use when the application item being discussed is an archive.
explicitly stated restrictions: No retention, storage, or database semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: A Layout is an IT-interface designed for specific roles, actors or individuals. The layout describes the content of logical and navigational patterns. The layout is then linked to the desired action. The layout may be created or serve as a template once it has been implemented in the desired IT environment. (Graphical User Interface or GUI, telephony with synthetic voices, WEB/Internet, etc.) Naming: A Layout specifies a GUI window. Use a name suited to the user’s interactive formula.
records.normalized explanation: An IT interface for roles, actors, or individuals, describing logical content and navigation and linked to an Action.
records.visible symbol description: White rectangular GUI window with a blue title bar.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: Linked to the desired Action; may become a reusable template after implementation.
explicitly allowed uses: Design for specific roles, actors, or individuals.
Describe logical content and navigational patterns.
Link to the desired action.
May serve as a template after implementation.
Name as a GUI window using a user-suited interactive formula.
explicitly stated restrictions: Examples of environment are illustrative and do not define renderer or application schemas.

records.verbatim definition: Notes is/are an abstract object(s) for noting general or specific opportunities or problems that are of interest and that are not naturally specified elsewhere. Named after the title of the identified opportunity or problem.
records.normalized explanation: A general-purpose annotation item for opportunities or problems not naturally specified elsewhere.
records.visible symbol description: Purple question mark and exclamation mark pair.
records.context or perspective: General or specific opportunity or problem context.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No hierarchy or containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Record opportunities or problems of interest not naturally specified elsewhere.
Name after the identified opportunity or problem.
explicitly stated restrictions: Use for matters not naturally specified elsewhere.

records.verbatim definition: Time Object is used to show date/time when processes and activities are to be executed, or when business objects are to be accessible/available.
records.normalized explanation: A date/time item for process or activity execution or Business object availability.
records.visible symbol description: Clock face with yellow bell or alert overlay.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Show when processes and activities are to execute.
Show when Business objects are accessible or available.
explicitly stated restrictions: No duration, recurrence, or timezone semantics are stated.

records.verbatim definition: Location is a physical place.
records.normalized explanation: A physical place.
records.visible symbol description: Purple map-pin or location marker.
records.hierarchy or containment meaning: No hierarchy or containment meaning is explicitly stated.
explicitly allowed uses: Represent a physical place.
explicitly stated restrictions: No coordinates, address schema, or geographic containment rules are stated.
